party_source: AEC SenateFirstPrefsByStateByVoteTypeDownload (the party name printed on the ballot); 'Independent' and blank are null.
instruction_source: AEC, 'How to make your vote count' (sample Senate ballot paper), https://www.aec.gov.au/Voting/How_to_vote/files/how-to-make-your-vote-count.pdf, read 2026-10-20.
instruction: You may vote in one of two ways. Either: Above the line, by numbering at least 6 of these boxes in the order of your choice (with number 1 as your first choice). Or: Below the line, by numbering at least 12 of these boxes in the order of your choice (with number 1 as your first choice).
notes: All formal ballots. ABOVE-THE-LINE VOTES ARE EXPANDED: a ballot numbering groups A, C is written as group A's candidates in ballot order, then group C's, as the official count treats it. So ballot lengths here are NOT what voters wrote; use the -btl and -atl files for that. AEC formal preferences file aec-senate-formalpreferences-20499-TAS.zip: 339,159 formal ballot papers, 95,385 below the line and 243,774 above the line. Cleanup follows the Commonwealth Electoral Act 1918 (see data/ausenate/README.md): a below-the-line vote numbering at least 1 to 6 is used as marked, up to the first missing or repeated number; otherwise the above-the-line marks are used the same way. blank_ballots holds all 12,221 informal ballots from the AEC (not only blank ones). Official winners in order of election, from SenateSenatorsElectedDownload. The Senate count uses the weighted inclusive Gregory method with bulk exclusions.
